newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota budget plan has $89.6 mln of GO bonds.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota budget plan has $89.6 mln of GO bonds.

text.p: Minnesota lawmakers approved $89.625 million of projects financed by general obligation bonds in their proposed budget this week, much of it for a new state revenue department building, a legislative aide said Tuesday.

Legislators on Monday approved spending $74.95 million for a new building to be located near the capitol building in St. Paul or in a suburb of the city, said Patricia Lindgren, house capital investment committee administrator.
Another $4 million has been allocated to a federal matching fund program to buy more than 1,000 houses as part of a levee relocation effort in reaction to the spring floods, Lindgren said.

Lindgren said bond proceeds would also fund a $4.5 million consolidation of community and technical college campuses in the northern Minnesota city of Hibbing. Another $4 million of proceeds would go to partly fund a wastewater treatment facility loan program, she said.
Legislators also approved $13.6 million of general fund appropriations and $7.8 million from motor vehicle transfer fees.
The spending plan has been forwarded to Gov. Arne Carlson, who is expected to sign it, Lindgren said.
